policy.purpose: Core (1A) is the difficulty-aware, prior-knowledge-aware subtopic-bucket teaching layer between source/Core (1) semantics and Core (2) transfer.
policy.primary_question_rule: Each Revised Core (2) v2 question belongs to exactly one primary SBA bucket; secondary prerequisites may be attached separately.
policy.production_selection_rule: For the current build queue, do not publish a dedicated SBA PDF when core2_primary_questions is empty; retain the bucket in the chapter map as SKIP_NO_PRIMARY_CORE2.
policy.priority_rule: Prioritise MEDIUM/HARD buckets for learners at or below 50% usable prior knowledge; increase visual staging, prerequisite rebuilding and worked-example guidance as readiness falls.
policy.core2_hint_preteach_rule: Every Core (2) H1/H2/H3 reveal must trace to an earlier Core (1A) learning atom and to an example/check; a question may be held until its release prerequisite buckets are complete.
policy.teaching_sequence_rule: Foundation/pretraining -> story/phenomenon -> staged picture -> what changed physically -> picture-to-maths bridge -> worked example -> guided/faded practice -> retrieval gate -> Core (2).

buckets.learner_title: Horizontal launch and launch from height
buckets.production_reason: Has primary Revised Core (2) questions; high question load requires several transfer families.

learning_atoms.title: Horizontal launch starts with one velocity component
learning_atoms.purpose: Establish u_y=0 at launch while gravity immediately creates vertical motion.
teaching_moves: contrast initial vertical velocity with later vertical motion
checks: state the launch components and accelerations without looking

learning_atoms.title: Vertical fall determines the shared event time
learning_atoms.purpose: Teach that the vertical drop fixes t first for a pure horizontal launch, then the same t is used in x-motion.
teaching_moves: show horizontal launch and free-fall shadow
reuse same t in x=u_x t
misconceptions: larger horizontal speed changes the fall time
checks: find fall time from height before using horizontal motion

learning_atoms.title: Impact velocity is rebuilt from components
learning_atoms.purpose: Combine constant v_x with gravity-built v_y to obtain impact speed, direction and component-ratio events.
teaching_moves: draw v_x and downward v_y at impact
translate verbal component ratios into equations
checks: construct impact speed and angle from given components

learning_atoms.title: Target geometry gives a displacement vector
learning_atoms.purpose: Distinguish curved path from straight displacement and use target geometry before dynamics when available.
teaching_moves: draw Delta x and Delta y triangle
checks: use target geometry to connect Delta x and Delta y

learning_atoms.title: Unequal-height launch requires a signed vertical landing equation
learning_atoms.purpose: Teach y=y0+u_y t-1/2 gt^2 with an explicit coordinate frame when launch and landing heights differ.
misconceptions: T=2u_y/g gives total time to lower ground
checks: write the correct signed landing equation for a tower problem

learning_atoms.title: Downward projection begins with a signed vertical component
learning_atoms.purpose: Handle u_y<0 cleanly when +y is upward and show an equivalent downward-positive convention.
teaching_moves: contrast with a consistent downward-positive form
misconceptions: downward means every term is negative
checks: assign signs from the axis, not from words

learning_atoms.title: Opposite horizontal launches share one vertical clock
learning_atoms.purpose: Use identical vertical motion to establish common fall time, then combine opposite horizontal motions through separation speed.
teaching_moves: draw two opposite launches from one height
checks: explain why only horizontal separation changes

learning_atoms.title: Units, ratios and scaling must be translated before substitution
learning_atoms.purpose: Prevent unit-system errors and teach verbal velocity ratios and horizontal-launch scaling.
checks: audit units and translate a component ratio before calculating
